extracted.intended_audience: patent and trademark attorneys, in-house IP counsel, and applicants filing or litigating patents/trademarks in Paraguay and Uruguay
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of prosecution and litigation rules, standards, and practical recommendations for patents (and related trademark notes) in Paraguay and Uruguay, aimed at practitioners preparing filings or enforcement actions in those jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to patent shall be the new inventions of products and procedures implying inventive activity and which shall be subject to industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentability requires novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness) and industrial application/applicability. This framing applies to both Paraguay and Uruguay as stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designs and utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility Models are patentable and Industrial Designs are protected by registration (distinct from patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility models: new dispositions or conformations entailing an improvement in use or function; require novelty and a minimum inventive activity. Uruguay and Paraguay each have distinct laws and regulatory decrees governing these rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software patents policy
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Software per se' is excluded from patentability; claims comprising embedded software in a system or in a specific step of a method are usually accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer-implemented inventions can be patentable if tied to a system or method; standalone software should be protected by copyright rather than patent. Uruguay references specific statutory exclusion ('software per se').

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Markush claims may be admitted if they meet the requirements for patentability (novelty, inventive step and industrial application), present a sufficient support in the specification, and properly characterize representative compounds of the various embodiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chemical/pharmaceutical claim drafting should ensure adequate support in the description and proper characterization of representative compounds to satisfy examination guidelines (Uruguay explicitly accepts Markush claims with sufficient support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological material deposit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the invention refers to biological material not publicly available and cannot be described so a person skilled in the art can perform it, the description shall be supplemented by deposit of such material in a recognized depositary institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide deposit accession data and copy of deposit at filing if material not public. Uruguay accepts Budapest Treaty deposits; include institution name, accession number and copies as needed; ensure specification enables reproduction when material is available or provide deposit information when not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linkage system status
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no Linkage System in Paraguay (and no linkage described for Uruguay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent enforcement is not tied to drug regulatory approval procedures in these jurisdictions; no patent-listing-for-market-approval linkage reflected in local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty – definition and prior art scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is novel if there is no previous record thereof in the state of the prior art. The state of the prior art encompasses anything disclosed or made accessible to the public anywhere in the world prior to the filing date (or applicable priority date), including publications, oral disclosure, sale, use, or other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published patent applications in prosecution before the local Office count as prior art to the extent the content is included in the earlier application when published. There is a limited grace exception for disclosures by the inventor or derived from illegal acts within the year preceding filing (Paraguay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (non-obviousness) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be deemed to have inventive step if, for a person skilled in the relevant technical matter, it would not be obvious or derived in an evident manner from the state of the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners assess whether claimed advances would be obvious to a skilled person in view of prior art. Apply standard country practice and supporting evidence where inventive contribution is close to known techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting — preamble and technical characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be formulated with a preamble indicating the object of the invention and the required technical characteristics for defining the elements claimed that combined form part of the state of the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claims to clearly separate known/prior-art features (preamble or first part) from the novel/characterizing features (characterized part) as adapted to PY PTO practice. Ensure the preamble and characterizing portions together define the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and support of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should be clear, the first claim should be independent and include relevant features; other claims should be subordinated. Claims should have support in the specification as filed originally when the application was filed in Paraguay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague expressions (e.g., 'about', 'effective amount') and unquantified qualifiers. Include dependent claims as needed. There is no formal limit to the number of claims but they must correspond to the nature of the invention and be supported by the original filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paraguayan 'Characterized' claim format
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should be characterized to be adapted to PY PTO practice, having a first part in which the prior art features are described, and a 'Characterized' part in which the relevant features of the invention are detailed and for which protection is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the two-part claim format (known features / characterized features) commonly expected by PY examiners to ease prosecution and demonstrate differentiation from prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method and process claims patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and process claims are considered patentable in Paraguay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft method/process claims with clear steps and technical effect; they are treated as patentable subject matter provided other patentability requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required filing documents (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required documents: a) Power of Attorney certified by Notary Public within 60 days; b) Complete name and address of applicant; c) Complete name and address of inventor; d) Inventor's assignment certified by Notary Public within 90 days; e) Certified copy of priority document and Spanish translation within 90 days; f) Title, Specification, abstract, drawings and claims in Spanish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely file all formal documents and Spanish translations per deadlines to avoid formal objections or loss of rights; ensure notarization and certified copies where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: SME filing benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no SME (small and medium entity) benefits in Paraguay Patent regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect fee reductions or special procedural advantages for SMEs under Paraguayan patent law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition / third-party observations (pre-grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no formal opposition system in Paraguay; however, the law admits pre-grant third-party observations after publication. Any interested party may submit observations prior to availability examination; filing observations does not suspend proceedings and the applicant is not a party to the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party observations can be used to bring evidence of lack of patentability to the Office's attention but will not turn the applicant into an opposing party; applicants may file responses once notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews with examiners are allowed in practice and are very helpful during prosecution in Paraguay. Examiner interviews are allowed and are helpful to overcome office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interviews to clarify claim scope, present arguments, and negotiate allowable claim language; schedule and prepare written records where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary divisional applications of pending patent applications are allowed in Paraguay. Applicants can file voluntary divisional applications at any time during prosecution of the parent case (before granting). Traditionally, divisionals are filed under Examiner's request due to lack of unity objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File divisionals before grant if needed to pursue distinct inventions; watch for unity objections and examiner prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection provided by pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent rights are only enforceable in Paraguay once the patent has been granted by the Patent Office. There is no enforceability between filing date and granting date (no provisional protection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on pending application for enforcement; consider alternative measures (precautionary remedies) but substantive patent rights arise only at grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are protected, after grant, for 20 years counted from the application date. Utility Models are protected for 10 years. There is no provision in Paraguayan Patent Law regarding term extensions due to prosecution delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan global patent term strategies accordingly; no local patent term adjustment/extension mechanism available in Paraguay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional applications have not been regulated in Paraguayan patent law; similarly, provisional applications not regulated under Paraguayan Trademark Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect a formal provisional filing route analogous to some other jurisdictions; use priority claims from foreign provisional filings according to deadlines and required certified copies/translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no regulation regarding expedited examination in Paraguay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No formal fast-track procedure; plan prosecution timelines accordingly and consider strategic filings in other offices if expedited examination is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendments — no new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applicants can amend the application claims if requested by the PY PTO examiner or to answer an office action; new subject matter cannot be incorporated at any stage, neither in the Specification nor in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend only to correct errors or respond to objections; ensure any amendment is fully supported by the original filing to avoid adding new matter and potential invalidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive rights conferred by patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent grants exclusive rights to exploit the invention: for a product, prevent third parties from fabricating, using, offering for sale, selling or importing; for a procedure, prevent use of the procedure and acts of use, offering for sale, sale or import of products directly obtained through the procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claim scope to align with anticipated enforcement goals; understand that unauthorized acts beyond exceptions may be considered infringing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributory infringement and criminal/administrative remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Paraguayan patent law does not mention contributory infringement; there are no criminal or administrative actions available (in Paraguay) and no judicial precedents regarding contributory infringements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on civil remedies; contributory liability doctrines are not established and likely require judicial development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing to sue
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner is entitled to bring infringement action. In case of a contractual licensed patent, the licensee may be entitled to bring suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure license agreements expressly confer enforcement rights if licensee enforcement is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precautionary measures and interim reliefs
rubrics_metrics.description: The judge, at the request of the plaintiff, may order precautionary measures to prevent greater damages, obtain or preserve proof, assure effectiveness of the action, recover damages and prevent further infringements. Precautionary measures may be requested prior to initiating the infringement action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available measures include immediate cessation of infringing acts, garnishment/seizure of infringing products and materials, and suspension of importation/exportation. Bonds are required and measures can be granted ex parte with prompt notice to defendant; affected party can request reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonds for precautionary measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonds are requested to grant precautionary measures or injunctions and will only be executed once the patent holder deposits the bond determined by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to post security to obtain preliminary reliefs; courts determine bond amount based on case specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information disclosure orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent judicial authority may, at any time in the proceedings, order the defendant to provide information regarding persons who may have participated in the production or marketing of the infringing products or procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts can compel disclosure of supply chain and third-party data to aid enforcement and damage calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute of limitations for patent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The action for infringement shall be subject to limitation in two years as from the date that the owner becomes aware of the infringement, or four years since the infringement was last committed, between them the one that expires first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt monitoring and enforcement are required; choose filing timing carefully relative to discovery of infringement and last infringing act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation and invalidity counterclaims
rubrics_metrics.description: The defendant may file a counterclaim for invalidity of the patent and offer evidence that the invention lacks novelty, inventive step or industrial application; both actions will be decided in the same resolution on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect invalidity defenses to be litigated jointly with infringement allegations; prepare robust prior art and technical rebuttals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witnesses and depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Witness depositions are not usually proposed as evidence in infringement patent lawsuits; witnesses are not commonly used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely more on documentary, technical and expert evidence rather than testimonial depositions in Paraguay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages and litigation costs (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may claim compensation for damages; 'punitive damages' are not provided. Losing party will have to pay attorney’s fees of the counterparty, and the amount will be set by the Judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate expected recoverable damages under local law and be prepared for judge-determined attorney fee awards rather than statutory multipliers or punitive awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery / pre-trial procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no discovery in Paraguay. Pre-trial preliminary measures aimed at preserving evidence or obtaining documents can be requested to the judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preliminary evidence preservation measures and local procedural tools rather than U.S.-style discovery; plan evidence preservation before enforcement actions commence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary support and burden of proof (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: In civil proceedings the judge may require the defendant prove that an identical product has not been obtained by use of the patented procedure; courts rely on technical experts and documents proposed by parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect technical, documentary and expert evidence; plaintiffs bear the initial burden to show infringement but courts may shift evidentiary obligations to defendants in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges' IP expertise (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil and Commercial courts are the competent courts to decide patent litigations. The overall IP expertise of the judges is rather low due to relatively few patent litigation cases and precedents in Paraguay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to explain technical issues in accessible terms and support submissions with neutral expert reports to assist judges unfamiliar with complex patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges support their decisions mainly on opinions from technical experts appointed by the court and documents obtained from official or private institutions proposed by the parties and authorized by the court. Technical evidence and expert advice are highly advisable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively submit persuasive expert reports and propose qualified experts; courts value technical expertise and often appoint or rely on experts in decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal liability for patent infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no personal liability on patent infringements followed against corporations, nor personal liability on adverse resolution on the merits for corporation executives. Individuals that are defendants on patent infringement actions may have to pay the plaintiff's attorneys fees if found responsible. There is personal liability for patent infringement if found guilty in criminal procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporate officers typically insulated from civil liability absent criminal findings; evaluate criminal prosecution risk separately where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust issues related to enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendants may use a patent enforcement action to complain before antitrust authorities, but there is no precedent of any antitrust resolution derived from patent infringement actions in Paraguay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of antitrust risk in enforcement strategies but note absence of precedent in local practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark types and registrable forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademarks may be nominative, figurative, combined and three-dimensional; may consist of words, emblems, monograms, stamps, vignettes, embossments, names, fantasy words, letters and numbers, combinations, color displays, labels, containers, wrappings, shape/presentation/conditioning of products or means/places of sale. Non-traditional trademarks (audible, olfactory, taste) are allowed in Paraguay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing trademark filings consider non-traditional forms and ensure distinctiveness for less common marks; provide appropriate specimens and descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unregistrable marks — categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Article lists marks that may not be registered, including signs inducing error about nature/properties/origin; reproduction/imitation of a third party's notorious sign causing confusion or exploiting notoriety; national or foreign denominations/insignias used by states and international bodies; usual/necessary form of products; a single colour; names/words already in general use; trademarks identical or similar to existing registrations for same goods/services; pseudonym/portrait without consent; geographical indications; signs applied by those without right to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate absolute and relative grounds for refusal; research prior registrations and notoriety; obtain consents where required (e.g., portraits or names).

rubrics_metrics.name: Famous and well-known marks protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Famous and well-known marks are protected according to the Paris Convention and TRIPS Agreement rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim fame/well-known status where applicable to seek broader protection and prevent dilution or exploitation of notoriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness and confusing similarity criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademarks must not be visually, phonetically and ideologically similar. Factors include type of consumer, whether marks are famous, prior coexistence in the market, inclusion of common ingredients, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess likelihood of confusion holistically, considering consumer sophistication and market context; prepare arguments on fame, coexistence and differences where opposition or examination raises similarity issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark application formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: File an application for each class including applicant name/address, description of trademark and indication of products/services, and Power of Attorney (signature certified by notary public).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with formal requirements and class selections; notarized POAs and accurate descriptions facilitate prosecution and avoid formal rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark rights and enforceability timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark rights are only enforceable in Argentina/Paraguay once the trademark has been granted by the Trademark Office. There is no enforceability between the filing date and granting date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on pending trademark applications for enforcement; consider coexistence/monitoring strategies until registration is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark opposition system (pre-grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paraguayan Trademark regulation provides a pre-grant opposition system. Any person is entitled to file opposition on a trademark application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor publications and be prepared to file oppositions or responses; oppositions can extend prosecution timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional applications have not been regulated under Paraguayan Trademark Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No formal provisional trademark regime; file complete applications and manage priority from foreign filings per required evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark litigation venue and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: In Paraguay, infringement actions are filed before Civil and Commercial Courts (no administrative infrigement procedure). Preliminary injunctions and other pre-trial/interim reliefs may be requested, including ex-parte remedies; bonds are requested for temporary injunctions and are executed once deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for court remedies and bond postings for interim relief; no specialized administrative enforcement track exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark statute of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark infringement actions can be started during the period the trademark is being infringed and until two years after the last infringement act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of the two-year window following last act for bringing claims; track ongoing infringement to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark evidentiary support and burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden of proof of infringement lies on the trademark owner. Expert evidence and witness testimony are not usually used; judges experienced with trademark cases may not rely heavily on experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare strong documentary evidence of infringement and market use; expert reports are less common but may be used where complex technical or consumer perception issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark damages and litigation costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark owner may claim compensation for damages; 'punitive damages' are not provided. The losing party is obliged to support the attorney fees determined by the Judge: between 5% and 20% of the amounts discussed in court. If no monetary amount is involved, Judges usually fix attorney fees considering complexity and duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate likely attorney fee awards and consider economic scale of the dispute; statutory punitive damages are not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal liability for trademark infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no personal liability on trademark infringements followed against corporations, nor personal liability on adverse resolution on the merits for corporate executives. Individuals that are defendants may have to pay plaintiff's attorneys fees if found responsible. There is personal liability in criminal procedures if found guilty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil exposure typically affects the corporate entity; criminal routes present different personal liability risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark fee shifting practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The losing party is obliged to support the attorney fees determined by the Judge (between 5% and 20% of the amounts discussed in court). If no amount is involved, Judges set attorney fees considering complexity and duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect judge-discretionary fee awards rather than fixed statutory scales; factor potential fee recovery into litigation strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain name registration criteria (Paraguay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Domain names in Paraguay can be registered before NIC Paraguay; the criterion for domain registration is first-come, first-served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register country-code domains promptly to secure online identifiers; first-come-first-served means priority is based on filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and appellate practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolutions on the merits from First Instance courts may be appealed to Appeals courts (Second Instance); appellate procedure durations vary (patents and trademarks have multi-year timelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for multi-stage litigation timelines: typical patent first instance 3–6 years, second instance 1–3 years; trademark first instance 2–5 years, second instance 1–2 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement and alternative dispute resolution usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Settlement can be reached at any stage of the process. Arbitration and mediation are not legal resources usually used for IP in Paraguay (and ADR not commonly used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While ADR is available in principle, local practice favors court resolution; consider settlement where timely relief or confidentiality is important.
